extraction.plan_title: Café Tenant Improvement - Floor Plan B
extraction.scale_note: All dimensions printed; do not scale.
uncertainties: Restroom room dimensions are not printed.

findings.detail: Your plan shows 1 exit. A space for 106 people needs 2.
findings.fix: Place it far from the one you have, or make the public area smaller so the space holds 49 people or fewer.
findings.reviewed_by: SDCI Ordinance (building code) review, SBC Ch. 10 Means of Egress
findings.title: Add a second exit

findings.citation: Seattle Mechanical Code 507 (Type I hood over grease- or smoke-producing appliances); Seattle Fire Code 904 (hood fire suppression)
findings.detail: Your plan doesn't show a Type I exhaust hood with fire suppression. Cooking that makes grease or smoke needs one.
findings.fix: Add a Type I hood and suppression system over the cooking line, or limit the menu to equipment that does not need one.
findings.title: Add a Type I hood over the cooking line

findings.detail: Your plan says there are no sprinklers. This Group A-2 space needs them: 106 people, which is 100 or more (limit: 100 people or 5,000 sq ft).
findings.fix: Ask the landlord whether the building has sprinklers and note it on the plan. If it has none, budget for a system or plan for fewer people.
findings.reviewed_by: Seattle Fire Department review, SBC Ch. 9 Fire Protection
findings.title: Add a sprinkler system

findings.detail: Your plan shows this exit door swinging inward. A space for 106 people needs exit doors that swing out, the way people leave.
findings.fix: Re-hang the door to swing outward. Check that it doesn't block the sidewalk or a required clear space.
findings.reviewed_by: SDCI Ordinance (building code) review, SBC Ch. 10 Means of Egress
findings.title: Turn the exit door to swing outward: Door 1

findings.detail: Your plan shows 30 in. clear. A door needs at least 32 in.
findings.fix: Widen the opening to at least 32 in. clear. A 36 in. door usually gives this.
findings.reviewed_by: SDCI Ordinance (building code) review, SBC Ch. 10 Means of Egress
findings.title: Widen the door: Restroom 1 door (Restroom 1)

findings.detail: Your plan shows 30 in. clear. A door needs at least 32 in.
findings.fix: Widen the opening to at least 32 in. clear. A 36 in. door usually gives this.
findings.reviewed_by: SDCI Ordinance (building code) review, SBC Ch. 10 Means of Egress
findings.title: Widen the door: Restroom 2 door (Restroom 2)

findings.detail: Your plan shows no exit signs. Each of the 2 exits needs one.
findings.fix: Add an illuminated exit sign at each required exit.
findings.reviewed_by: SDCI Ordinance (building code) review, SBC Ch. 10 Means of Egress
findings.title: Add an exit sign at each exit

findings.detail: Your plan shows 30 in. A wheelchair route needs at least 36 in.
findings.fix: Move furniture or fixtures to give 36 in. clear.
findings.reviewed_by: SDCI Ordinance (building code) review, SBC Ch. 11 Accessibility
findings.title: Widen the aisle: Aisle A (between tables)

findings.citation: SBC Chapter 11 / ICC A117.1; ADA 304.3.1 and 603.2.1
findings.detail: Your plan shows 54 in. of clear floor. A wheelchair needs 60 in. to turn.
findings.fix: Enlarge the room or rearrange fixtures to clear a 60 in. circle.
findings.reviewed_by: SDCI Ordinance (building code) review, SBC Ch. 11 Accessibility
findings.title: Widen the restroom so a wheelchair can turn: Restroom 1

findings.citation: SBC Chapter 11 / ICC A117.1; ADA 304.3.1 and 603.2.1
findings.detail: Your plan shows 54 in. of clear floor. A wheelchair needs 60 in. to turn.

findings.title: Widen the restroom so a wheelchair can turn: Restroom 2

findings.citation: King County Board of Health Code Titles 5 and R5; Washington State Retail Food Code (chapter 246-215 WAC). Plan review by Public Health - Seattle & King County.
findings.detail: Your plan doesn't show a handwashing sink in the prep area. Food prep needs its own hand sink.
findings.fix: Add a hand sink in the prep area (separate from the dish sink).
findings.reviewed_by: Public Health - Seattle & King County food plan review (separate from SDCI)
findings.rule_source: King County Board of Health Code Title 5; WAC 246-215
findings.title: Add a handwashing sink in the food prep area

findings.detail: Your plan doesn't mark accessible seats. 3 of your 56 seats need to be at accessible tables.
findings.fix: Mark accessible tables (knee clearance, 28-34 in. surface height) on the plan.
findings.reviewed_by: SDCI Ordinance (building code) review, SBC Ch. 11 Accessibility
findings.title: Mark the accessible seats

findings.citation: Seattle Fire Code 906.1; Class K at commercial cooking, 906.4
findings.detail: Your plan doesn't show fire extinguishers. Each floor needs at least one within 75 ft of travel.
findings.fix: Show extinguisher locations; add a Class K unit at the cooking line.
findings.reviewed_by: Seattle Fire Department review, SBC Ch. 9 Fire Protection
findings.title: Show the fire extinguishers

findings.citation: SBC 303.1.1 (assembly use with occupant load under 50 is classified Group B); SBC Chapter 3 for Groups A-2, A-3, B and M
findings.detail: Your plan holds 106 people. The building code puts a café or restaurant that size in Group A-2.
findings.reviewed_by: SDCI Ordinance (building code) review, SBC Ch. 3 Occupancy
findings.title: Occupancy classification

findings.citation: SBC Table 2902.1; SBC 2902.1.1 (50/50 split); SBC 2902.2 exceptions 2, 3, 4 and 7 (when one shared toilet room is allowed)
findings.detail: Your plan shows 2 toilets. A space for 106 people needs 2 (A-2 restaurants: 1 for men and 1 for women).
findings.reviewed_by: SDCI Ordinance (building code) review, SBC Ch. 29 Plumbing Systems
findings.title: Toilet count

findings.citation: Seattle Municipal Code Title 23 (Land Use Code); SMC 23.47A
findings.detail: Neighborhood Commercial 2. Most uses are limited to 25,000 sq ft. A restaurant is generally allowed. This plan is 2,400 sq ft, within the 25,000 sq ft limit. Confirm overlays, pedestrian-street rules and any change-of-use requirement.
findings.title: Zoning: NC2-55 (M)
